tools.name: create_post
tools.description:
Create and publish a post to one or more social media platforms immediately.

Octopost handles formatting, auth and uploads. Which networks work today is in the server instructions (and get_guide topic "platforms").

tools.name: schedule_post
tools.description:
Schedule a post for future publishing. The Octopost scheduler will publish it at the specified time automatically.

The post is saved as a draft until the scheduled time, then published to all specified platforms.

Same platform limits and same options as create_post, which documents them in full. O

tools.name: list_posts
tools.description: List posts, newest first: content preview, platforms, status, scheduled time and each network's link. Filter with status. Results are paged: when next_cursor is set, call again with cursor = next_cursor for the next page. Call get_post for one post's full details.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description:
List all connected social media accounts. ALWAYS call this before create_post to see which platforms the user has connected.

Returns each account's platform, handle, id, and whether it is the platform's default (used when a post names no account). A platform can have several accounts: pass "account

tools.name: get_post
tools.description: Get everything about one post: status, full text, thread segments, per-network variants, media (with alt text), queue status and position, which account posts on each network, per-network results with links, and the last error. Use it to check whether a post went out everywhere.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description:
Get a comprehensive guide on using Octopost effectively. Returns platform limits, best practices, content tips, and feature documentation. Call this if you need help with:
- What platforms are supported and their limits
- How to format content for cross-platform posting
- Media/image/video requireme

tools.name: update_post
tools.description:
Update a post's content, platforms, scheduled time, attached media, or thread reply segments. Only works on unpublished posts (drafts, scheduled, queued, and pending).

Any field you omit is preserved as-is. Pass `media_urls: []` to clear all attached media; pass new media_urls or video_url to repla

tools.name: delete_post
tools.description:
Delete a post from Octopost. For published posts, also attempts to delete from each platform via their APIs.

Platform deletion support:
- Twitter: Full API deletion supported.
- Bluesky: Full API deletion supported (deleteRecord).
- LinkedIn: Full API deletion supported.
- Mastodon: Full API deleti

tools.name: retry_failed
tools.description:
Retry publishing to platforms that failed on a previous post. Only retries platforms that had errors — already-successful platforms are not re-published.

Call get_post first to see which platforms failed and why. You can retry all failed platforms or specify specific ones.

tools.name: cancel_scheduled
tools.description:
Cancel a scheduled post, converting it to a draft. The post is kept in Octopost but will NOT be published at the scheduled time.

Give it a new time later with reschedule_post. To publish it right away instead, call publish_draft.

tools.name: reschedule_post
tools.description:
Change the scheduled time of a post. The new time must be in the future. Works on both scheduled posts and drafts (effectively scheduling a draft).

The post will be published at the new time by Octopost's scheduler (checks every 60 seconds).

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: List publishing presets: saved platform combinations (system presets plus the user's own) with their cross-link settings. The create tools take platforms, not a preset name, so pass a preset's `platforms` (and cross-link fields) to create_post / schedule_post / queue_post. Platforms Octopost doesn't

tools.name: queue_post
tools.description:
Add a post to your publishing queue. It will be published automatically during your active hours. Posts require platforms to be specified.

HUMAN APPROVAL: set needs_approval=true when a person should review the post first (anything the user hasn't seen word for word). The post is held as "pending"

tools.name: approve_queued_post
tools.description: Approve a post that is waiting for approval. Approval is meant for a person: by default this tool refuses, and the post has to be approved from the email Octopost sent or the dashboard. It only works when the account owner turned on "Let agents approve posts made by a different agent" in Settings, a

tools.name: get_queue_status
tools.description: See your queue: how many posts are ready, how many need approval, when the next one publishes, and your queue settings.

tools.name: update_queue_settings
tools.description:
Change your queue settings: how often to post, active hours, timezone, or pause/resume the queue.

Defaults: publish every 4 hours, active 9am-8pm, timezone America/New_York. The queue only publishes during active hours. The exact minute within each interval is randomized so posts look natural.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description:
How published posts did: likes, reposts, replies, quotes and (on X) views.

Two modes:
- With post_id: that post's numbers per network, plus snapshots taken about 1 hour, 24 hours and 7 days after it went live.
- Without post_id: a summary of posts published between from and to (default: the last 30

tools.name: publish_draft
tools.description: Publish a post that's already saved in Octopost right now: a draft, a scheduled post (it goes out now instead of at its time) or a queued post (it skips the queue). Uses the post's own text, networks, media and thread segments. Returns per-network results like create_post (or status "publishing" if

tools.name: preview_post
tools.description: Dry run: what would happen if you sent this post, without saving or posting anything. Returns ok (would it go out), problems (fix these first) and warnings, character counts per network and part the way each network counts (X: links 23, emoji/CJK 2; Bluesky: graphemes), X units it would use vs what'

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: How much of the plan is used: X post units this month (used, limit, remaining, when it resets; a post with a link costs 13 units, a plain post 1), and connected accounts vs the plan's limit. A null limit means unlimited. Check it before a batch of X posts so you don't hit the cap part way.

tools.name: reject_queued_post
tools.description: Take a queued post out of the queue and turn it back into a draft, with an optional note saying why (shown with the post). tools.name: reorder_queue
tools.description: Set the order queued posts publish in. The posts you list go first, in that order; queued posts you leave out keep their current order after them. Pending-approval posts can be listed too: their place applies once approved. Call list_posts with status "queued" to see the queue.

tools.name: split_thread
tools.description: Split long text into thread parts that fit every network you name, breaking at paragraphs, then sentences, then words. Counts the way each network does (X: links are 23, emoji 2; Bluesky: graphemes). Nothing is saved or posted. Pass the result straight to create_post / schedule_post / queue_post as

tools.name: create_upload
tools.description: Attach a file from your machine (screenshot, photo, video): this returns a one-time upload_url, good for 15 minutes and one file. Send the raw bytes to it, e.g. curl -T ./shot.png "<upload_url>" (PUT; no auth header needed). The response has media_url: pass it in media_urls (as the URL, or {url, alt

tools.name: list_feeds
tools.description: List the RSS/Atom feeds this account turns into posts: each feed's networks, template, mode ("hold" = every new item waits for a person to approve it, "queue" = new items join the posting queue), how often it is checked, when it was last checked, any error, and how many items it has seen and posted.

tools.name: add_feed
tools.description:
Turn an RSS or Atom feed (a blog, a newsletter, a changelog) into posts. Octopost reads the feed right away (a site address works too if the page links its feed) and then checks it every 30 minutes by default. Each new item becomes a post from the template.

tools.name: remove_feed
tools.description: Stop turning a feed into posts and forget which items it has seen. Posts the feed already made (published, queued or waiting for approval) are kept; delete those separately with delete_post if needed. Get the feed id from list_feeds.

tools.name: set_evergreen
tools.description: Mark a post evergreen (or not). When the posting queue runs empty, Octopost posts an evergreen post again in the empty queue slot, picking the one that has rested longest. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_post" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_post, list_posts, list_accounts, get_post, get_guide, queue_post, approve_queued_post, get_queue_status, get_analytics, get_usage, reorder_queue, list_feeds, add_feed, remove_feed · Private data: schedule_post, delete_post, retry_failed, queue_post, create_upload · Public sink: create_post, schedule_post, list_posts, list_accounts, get_post, update_post, delete_post, retry_failed, cancel_scheduled, reschedule_post, queue_post, approve_queued_post, update_queue_settings, get_analytics, publish_draft, preview_post, get_usage, reject_queued_post, reorder_queue, create_upload, add_feed, set_evergreen · Destructive: get_guide, update_post, delete_post, preview_post, reject_queued_post, remove_feed.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
